thread:
alex: Thanks for the thoughtful questions in today's all-hands. Starting a short follow-up thread to capture decisions and owners for the runtime roadmap Q&A (performance, batching/caching, kernel rollout). Keep replies short so product/ops can act.
mina: first: public SLOs. We need exact numbers to put in the playbook and a short note about measurement windows and egress overhead. Can infra propose final numbers?
diego: proposal (internal): hosted p50=18ms, p95=110ms, p99=380ms. dedicated p50=12ms, p95=70ms, p99=220ms. Measurement window: 5m rolling, exclude warmup spikes during deploys. Note: add a footnote about regional egress +20ms.
sophia: second: fallback/rollback policy. We want deterministic, observable behavior: auto-fallback allowed only for best-effort routes. SLA routes require explicit opt-in for any downgrade. Every fallback must emit a trace and set header X-Model-Fallback. Also prefer quantized-same over smaller-architecture to avoid semantics.
rahul: ops asks: what are hard canary gates for kernel-v4? We need numbers for perf, memory, and quality to automate gating.
diego: agreed. Suggested gates: perf: p95 regression < 4% vs baseline on sampled traffic; memory: resident < +6% vs baseline on same traffic; quality: sampled-eval delta < 1.0 on our internal score. Determinism check: token-diff-rate < 0.2% on a 5k prompt sample. If any gate fails, auto-roll back.
mina: product wants a short customer-friendly blurb for release notes that explains fallback guarantees and how to opt into conservative routing. Can we get two sentences?
sophia: will draft two lines: 1) what best-effort means; 2) how SLA customers can pin models/no-fallback. Will post by EOD.
alex: batching knobs: clarifying adaptive vs fixed. We default to per-worker adaptive microbatching with a per-route max_batch_size and an opt-out header X-Request-Priority. Also a global circuit to prevent large batch buildup on sudden spikes. Example config we discussed:
```
batching:
  mode: adaptive
  per_worker_max: 64
  target_latency_ms: 50
  priority_header: X-Request-Priority
  spike_circuit_threshold: 70%_cpu
```
rahul: ops will run a 10-day experiment enabling adaptive per-worker microbatching on two canary clusters (max 32/64). Success criteria: p95 change within +/-5% for SLA routes and p95 improvement for non-SLA routes.
diego: KV cache strategy: we want hot-prefix sticky extension and per-tenant memory caps. Proposal: default TTL 5m, hot-score extends up to 4x TTL but bounded by per-tenant cap (default 5% node mem). Also implement LRU eviction with tenant fairness weights.
sophia: product question: can we expose cache_hit_rate per-route in console and an advisory when tenant eviction spikes? Customers want actionable metrics.
rahul: yes, platform will add cache_hit_rate and eviction_rate per-route and an alert when eviction_rate > 3x baseline for 1h.
alex: cost guardrails: if enabling hot-extend increases instance memory usage > 7% across fleet, auto-disable and surface to infra. Ops to measure cost delta during experiment.
mina: small process ask: please publish numeric thresholds for canary gates and fallback semantics in an RFC by Wednesday. That will unblock marketing/product copy and the console changes.
dieg o: typo fix: diego: will publish RFC with numbers and canned roll/rollback steps.
ops-bot: Meeting notes uploaded: https://redwood.internal/notes/allhands-2799990000. :white_check_mark:
alex: action items recap: 1) diego publish kernel-v4 RFC with numeric gates (diego) 2) ops run batching + hot-extend experiments and report (rahul) 3) platform add X-Model-Fallback header + console metrics backlog (platform) 4) product draft release-note blurb (sophia). Please update thread when each item is done.
